# API Requirements Quality Checklist: Consulta API y estadísticas sísmicas

**Purpose**: Review the completeness, clarity, consistency, and testability of API and browser-client requirements
**Created**: 2026-11-17
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] CHK001 Are all fields required in the event collection and each event feature explicitly enumerated, including timestamp units, coordinate order, nullability, and metadata? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001–FR-004]
- [x] CHK002 Does the health requirement define both the health response fields and the meaning of each HTTP status, including a missing last-ingestion value? [Gap, Spec §FR-007]
- [x] CHK003 Are the required statistical outputs fully enumerated, including hourly counts, country counts, magnitude/depth distributions, and historical comparison? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008]
- [x] CHK004 Does the specification define when a historical baseline is considered available and how partial historical coverage is represented? [Gap, Spec §FR-008–FR-010, Assumptions]
- [x] CHK005 Are API error response formats and public error details defined for invalid filters, database outages, and unexpected query failures? [Gap, Spec §FR-005, FR-011]
- [x] CHK006 Are client configuration requirements specific about the public API URL and any refresh setting while excluding credentials and tokens? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014, User Story 3]

## Requirement Clarity

- [x] CHK007 Are accepted ISO 8601 timestamp forms, timezone requirements, and behavior for invalid or timezone-free values specified? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-003]
- [x] CHK008 Is the combination rule for simultaneous time, magnitude, and country filters explicitly stated? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, FR-009]
- [x] CHK009 Are the allowed country identifier values and the response to an unknown identifier defined? [Gap, Spec §FR-003, FR-009]
- [x] CHK010 Are distribution bin boundaries, widths, inclusion rules, and the denominator for missing values specified in the requirements, rather than only in design artifacts? [Gap, Spec §FR-008–FR-009]
- [x] CHK011 Is the historical comparison formula precise about current-period duration, daily-rate normalization, and zero-baseline behavior? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-010, Assumptions]
- [x] CHK012 Is the production CORS origin's configuration source and behavior when it is absent or contains multiple origins described without allowing an origin wildcard? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012, Assumptions]

## Requirement Consistency

- [x] CHK013 Are unknown depth values consistently represented as null properties while preserving a valid GeoJSON position in every relevant requirement and contract? [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, FR-004]
- [x] CHK014 Are missing-value counts defined consistently with the rule that null magnitudes do not satisfy `min_mag`, including which population is counted? [Conflict, Spec §FR-004, FR-009]
- [x] CHK015 Do the empty-result, truncation, and statistics requirements consistently distinguish complete successful results from failures or partial samples? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005–FR-006, FR-015]
- [x] CHK016 Are the health rule for old or absent ingestion timestamps and the client's staleness warning rule consistent across user scenarios, edge cases, and functional requirements? [Consistency, Spec §User Story 2–3, Edge Cases, FR-007, FR-013]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [x] CHK017 Can each success criterion be objectively evaluated from a stated sample, expected result, or unambiguous pass condition? [Measurability, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [x] CHK018 Are the default event/statistics period and the historical comparison period explicit and consistent for requests that omit time filters? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, FR-009, Assumptions]

## Scenario and Edge Case Coverage

- [x] CHK019 Are malformed requests, database/schema failures, network errors, timeout, empty results, and recovery after a later successful client refresh all covered as distinct requirement scenarios? [Coverage, Spec §User Stories, Edge Cases, FR-005, FR-011, FR-013, FR-016–FR-017]
- [x] CHK020 Are the event-query and statistics behaviors for a complete absence of replay history distinct from a valid historical baseline with zero events? [Coverage, Gap, Spec §FR-008–FR-011]
- [x] CHK021 Are requirements for invalid, disallowed, or absent CORS origins sufficiently defined to distinguish browser access denial from an API query failure? [Coverage, Spec §FR-012]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [x] CHK022 Is the absence of a server-side latency, throughput, or dataset-size target an intentional scope decision, rather than an unresolved release expectation? [Assumption, Spec §Success Criteria, Assumptions]
- [x] CHK023 Are the security boundaries for public read access, CORS, secrets, and the absence of browser credentials consistently stated across all endpoints and client configuration? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, FR-012, FR-014]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [x] CHK024 Is the historical-data completeness dependency documented with a clear outcome when coverage of the comparison year cannot be established? [Dependency, Spec §FR-008–FR-010, Assumptions]
- [x] CHK025 Is the client work boundary explicit enough to separate transport/error handling from the later map, filters, charts, and table requirements? [Scope, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Reviewer evaluation completed 2026-11-17 against the current spec, plan, contracts, quickstart and API contract. CHK010, CHK019 and CHK021 were marked satisfied after their denominator/bin rules, malformed and recovery flows, and CORS configuration/denial behavior were specified across the relevant artifacts. All 25 criteria are currently satisfied at requirements quality; this does not indicate implementation completion.
- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
- Add review findings inline; IDs are sequential for reference.
